chunks: And one of his sayings (peace be upon him): He said to al-Burj ibn Musahir al-Ta'i, who had said it in a voice loud enough for him to hear:
"Judgment belongs only to Allah," and he was from the Kharijites.

key_terms.الْخَوَارِجِ: Al-Kharijites (a sect known for their slogan and rebellion)
key_terms.لَا حُكْمَ إِلَّا لِلَّهِ: La hukma illa lillah (Judgment belongs only to God)
key_terms.لِلْبُرْجِ بْنِ مُسْهِرٍ: Al-Burj ibn Musahir (the specific narrator mentioned)

ai.seo_question: What did the Kharijites mean by 'La hukm illa lillah' and how did Imam Ali respond?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (peace be upon him) addressed al-Burj ibn Musahir al-Ta'i, a prominent Kharijite, who loudly proclaimed 'La hukma illa lillah' (Judgment belongs only to God). While the phrase itself is true, the Kharijites used it to reject the authority of the Prophet and Imams in interpreting divine law, effectively limiting God's judgment to their own literalist understanding. This incident underscores the Shia scholarly distinction between the absolute sovereignty of God and the necessary role of the Ahl al-Bayt in elucidating His will.
